subject: Dedicated Capacity discovery recap — HealthSync
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated Capacity discovery recap — HealthSync

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the call today. Wanted to capture the key points we covered and next steps so everyone is aligned. If I missed anything or any detail needs correction, flag it and I’ll update.

TL;DR: HealthSync is a good fit for Redwood Dedicated based on required isolation, predictable peak TPS, and need for autoscaling/bursting during batch ingest windows. Next step: quick internal sizing + SOW draft for a 3-month POC.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Production pain: inference latency variability and cost spikes during nightly batch runs; current self-hosted infra is complex to manage and frequently needs manual intervention.
- Compliance/isolation: PHI-sensitive workloads require tenant isolation and tighter network controls (VPC-only access).
- Goal: predictable per-request latency (p95 < 120ms) and predictable monthly inference cost for budgeting.

Current stack
- Model infra: in-house inference on AWS EC2 G4/16-ish fleet, managed with a homegrown autoscaler.
- Orchestration: Kubernetes with custom sharding; model served via Triton for larger models and a mix of smaller PyTorch endpoints.
- Traffic profile: baseline 20–30 TPS with nightly batch peaks up to ~180–220 TPS for bulk clinical-text processing. Burst windows last 20–40 minutes.

Success criteria for a POC
- Meet p95 latency target of < 120ms for interactive traffic at baseline load.
- Support peak burst to ~220 TPS with controlled degradation policy and warm standby capacity.
- Maintain network isolation (VPC peering, IP allowlist) and integrate with HealthSync KMS for key management.
- Provide token-level cost reporting and per-route dashboards for the three top inference endpoints.

Preliminary Dedicated fit notes
- Dedicated Reserved GPU pools align with their predictability requirement. We can provision a pool sized for baseline throughput with burst cushions for the nightly batch windows.
- Autoscaling policy: suggest schedule-based warmup for nightly batch windows + reactive autoscaling with a hard cap and fallback model variants for graceful degradation.
- Isolation: VPC-only deployment with optional on-prem connector for audit tools; KMS integration possible during Private onboarding but for Dedicated we can support customer-managed keys via BYOK options.

Open questions we asked Jordan to confirm
1) Is the 220 TPS number a sustained peak or short spikes within the 20–40 minute window?
2) What is the acceptable RPO/RTO for batch jobs if we need to throttle?
3) Any specific compliance docs you’ll need during the POC (SOC2 evidence, network diagrams, penetration test reports)?

Proposed next steps
- Redwood: internal sizing + SOW + capacity estimate (I’ll send draft attachments). Target delivery: EOD Monday 3/23. (Attached: redwood_capacity_estimate_HealthSync_v1.xlsx, SOW draft.)
- HealthSync: confirm the burst profile detail above and whether procurement needs an initial MSA redline during POC.
- Schedule a technical working session next week with Rishi (SE) to walk deep on peak behavior and autoscaling knobs.

Thanks — happy to iterate.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Attachment: redwood_capacity_estimate_HealthSync_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)
Attachment: redwood_dedicated_sow_draft.pdf (PDF, 4 pages)

From: Jordan Alvarez <jordan.alvarez@healthsync.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated Capacity discovery recap — HealthSync

Marissa —

Great summary, thank you. Quick answers inline: 

1) The ~220 TPS is a sustained peak for about 15–25 minutes during our nightly jobs. We do see short spikes a bit above that but they’re typically smoothed by our current queueing.
2) For batch jobs, acceptable RTO is ~30 minutes; RPO is flexible as long as we don’t lose input data (we maintain durable queues). If throttled, we can stretch the window to 90 minutes in worst-case.
3) We’ll need SOC2 Type II evidence and network diagrams during POC. Pen test report is not required for POC but will be needed for production.

Also, procurement asked if we can get a short statement of work and a not-to-exceed cost estimate to begin internal approval. The SOW draft you attached looks fine as a starting point.

Happy to do a technical session next Wednesday (3/25) at 10am PT with Rishi.

Thanks,
Jordan
VP of Engineering | HealthSync
jordan.alvarez@healthsync.com | (206) 555-0117
